title: Reading retreat: inference micro-evals and kernel heuristics
content:
Context / why I did this retreat:
Wanted a focused ~48 hour sprint to collect quick, actionable ideas for lowering tail latency and per-token cost without regressing on helpfulness. Note: this is a scratchpad — rough summaries, instincts, and at the bottom a short experiment plan.

Quick thread of readings (sketch notes):
1) Kernel packing + small-batch latency blog (reading: "Blockwise kernel packing for small-batch attention", blog, 2025)
   - Main idea: pack variable-length sequences into a set of fixed-sized tiles for attention kernels to keep occupancy high while preserving per-request isolation.
   - Why it matters for us: our serving workload has long tail of tiny interactive requests and bursts of medium-length batched jobs (webhooks / ingestion). Kernel packing reduces wasted GPU cycles on small batches.
   - Questions: how compatible is this with our KV cache design? Packing implies re-ordering in time — we need stable KV indexing.
   - Quick takeaway: try a prototype that packs only cross-request attention (not KV) to observe latency P95 improvements at 1–4 request batch sizes.

2) Paper: "Micro-evals for human-in-the-loop regression detection" (conference workshop notes)
   - Approach: maintain a small, rapidly computed eval set keyed to product features (e.g., completions for help-center flows). Use human spot checks to flag silent regressions.
   - Practical: suggested eval size is 200 examples per route, compute offline nightly but surface rolling deltas to alerts.
   - How to use: wire to model rollout pipeline -> if quality drop > X and token cost change < Y, block rollout.

3) Short note: "Selective low-bit for KV values" (internal experiment log)
   - Idea: quantize only the stored KV values (not weights nor the current activations). Observed 12–18% memory saving and little immediate quality loss on short-context tasks.
   - Risk: precision loss accumulates for very long contexts. Need eviction policy checks.

4) Ops postmortem (reading: "regression last-week: unrelated perf blip")
   - Blip traced to tensor copy on CPU path for cold-start model variant. Root cause: missing fast-path for 4-bit kernels under our allocator.
   - Fixes queued in PR 1345. Keep watch on latency after merge.

Synthesis / my heuristics:
- If we can reduce per-token compute by ~10% for small batches without changing model outputs noticeably, that beats a 20% P95 improvement that comes at the cost of any repeatable quality regression. Prioritize small-but-safe changes.
- Separate storage-level optimizations (KV quantization, compression) from execution-level optimizations (packing, fused kernels). They have different failure modes and rollback vectors.
- Micro-evals should be route-aware and cheap; we don't need massive evals to catch catastrophic regressions.

Experiment plan (short, actionable)
1) Kernel-pack prototype (2-week spike)
   - Implement in runtime: packing for attention compute only; keep KV cache indexing unchanged.
   - Metric: tail latency P50/P95/P99 for interactive route with synthetic small-batch workload (1–4 reqs). Also watch token/sec and GPU utilization.
   - Success criteria: P95 improvement >= 10% with <=2% throughput drop.

2) KV-value selective quantization (1 week on bench + 1 week on canary)
   - Build offline conversion that quantizes only KV values to 8-bit-aware format with small dequant step.
   - Run per-route micro-evals for retrievalQA and chat flows (200 examples per route).
   - Canary on Dedicated pool with read-only traffic for 48–72 hours.

3) Micro-eval harness for rollouts (2 week infra + ongoing)
   - Prototype: per-route 200-example set, nightly run, and Slack alert if >5% metric drop (BLEU-like / embed sim / task-specific).
   - Integrate with rollout gate: soft-stop on first sign of regression, require manual review.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Talk to Evan about possible interference between packing and our current CUDA kernel selection logic. Evan: pinged in Slack @evan on 2025-10-03.
- Add a small synthetic workload generator that models single-user interactive traces (random prompt length 8–256, 60% < 64 tokens).
- Check PR 1345 once merged: measure cold-start latency on the canary stack.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How does packing interact with llm-level sampling determinism? If we reorder tile execution, do we risk non-deterministic RNG seeds affecting repeatability of outputs? (need to verify)
- What is the overhead of dequant per-request for KV selective quant? Might offset memory wins.

Random riffing (brainstorm mode):
- Could we do a hybrid cache: keep top-N recent KV entries in FP16 and older ones in 8-bit compressed? Evict based on recency and usefulness score.
- For micro-evals: track hallucination proxies (like factuality via external QA) for high-value routes; add prioritized human review.

References / links collected during retreat (raw):
- blockwise kernels blog: https://inference-kernel-lab.example/block-pack-2025
- micro-eval workshop notes: https://workshop.example/micro-evals-2025
- runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1345
- confluence mini-evals doc: https://confluence.internal/redwood/inference/mini-evals-2025

End of notes — will convert top section into a short proposal doc if any of the spike results look promising.

Personal meta: felt useful to code small prototypes in same day; helps sharpen what to ask infra team for. Keep these 48h retreats monthly.
